data.title: Civeo raises 2026 guidance to $710M-$720M revenue and $89M-$92M adjusted EBITDA as Canada momentum builds
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Civeo Corporation (CVEO) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "We had a solid third quarter, and we are raising our full year guidance." (CEO, President & Director Bradley Dodson)
  • "On the strength of our year-to-date performance, we are raising our 2026 revenue guidance to $710 million to $720 million and our adjusted EBITDA guidance to $89 million to $92 million." (CEO Dodson)
  • "Since the end of the second quarter, we have secured contracts with a diverse set of customers for the deployment of approximately 700 mobile camp fleet rooms across Canada." (CEO Dodson)
  • "For the first time in several years, the conversation with customers in the region is shifting from price concessions to asset availability." (CEO Dodson)
  • "Metallurgical coal prices are above $250 a ton, yet our customers are behaving as they would at much lower prices because of elevated diesel costs, broader inflation and higher royalties at these price levels are compressing margins." (CEO Dodson)
  • "Today, we reported total revenues in the third quarter of $193.1 million compared to $170.5 million in the third quarter of 2025, an increase of 13%." (Senior VP, CFO & Treasurer E. Gerry)
  • "Net income for the quarter was $5.2 million or $0.50 per diluted share compared to a net loss of $0.5 million or a net loss per share of $0.04 in the prior year period." (CFO Gerry)

Outlook

  • "Updated 2026 revenue guidance is $710 million to $720 million, up from $675 million to $700 million and updated adjusted EBITDA guidance is $89 million to $92 million, up from previous guidance of $85 million to $90 million." (CEO Dodson)
  • "We are also increasing our full year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to a range of $30 million to $35 million, which previously was $25 million to $30 million." (CEO Dodson)
  • "As usual, we expect the fourth quarter to be sequentially lower than the third, reflecting the end of turnaround season and holiday seasonality in Canada, along with normal December seasonality in Australia." (CEO Dodson)
  • "Our full year guidance also includes approximately $1 million of make-ready and mobilization expenses in the fourth quarter for new customer contracts in Canada." (CEO Dodson)
  • "On our mobile fleet, the approximately 700 rooms we have contracted are expected to deploy in late 2026 and the first quarter of 2027 with no meaningful contribution to 2026 revenues." (CEO Dodson)

Financial Results

  • "During the quarter, Civeo generated adjusted EBITDA of $30.1 million compared to $28.6 million in the third quarter of 2025, an increase of 5%." (CFO Gerry)
  • "Operating cash flow was $26.4 million compared to $13.8 million in the prior year period." (CFO Gerry)
  • "Third quarter revenues from our Australian segment were $129.5 million, up 4% from $124.5 million in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA was $23.2 million compared to $25 million in the prior year period." (CFO Gerry)
  • "Integrated services revenue was $73.1 million, up 11% in U.S. dollars and up approximately 2% in local currency." (CFO Gerry)
  • "Third quarter revenues were $63.6 million compared to $46 million in the third quarter of 2025, an increase of 38% or approximately 40% in local currency. Adjusted EBITDA was $11.1 million compared to $7.6 million in the prior year period, an increase of 47%." (CFO Gerry)
  • "As of September 30, 2026, we had $126.9 million of availability under our revolving credit facility. Total debt was $217.5 million, and net debt was $196 million... Our total net leverage ratio was 2.1x." (CFO Gerry)

Q&A

  • Stephen Gengaro, Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated: "What type of terms and kind of economic paybacks should we be thinking about?" Bradley Dodson: "All that expenditure... will all be captured well within the contract with less than a 1-year payback." (CEO Dodson)
  • Stephen Gengaro, Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated: "And then what other incremental capacity do you have that's deployable?" E. Gerry: "It's 6,000 to 7,000 installed lodge rooms..." (CFO Gerry)
  • James Rollyson, Raymond James & Associates: "Maybe just kind of help think through how you approach pricing as you scale the existing rooms out first" Bradley Dodson: "Term matters..." and "prices need to double. I think they need to at least double." (CEO Dodson)
  • James Rollyson, Raymond James & Associates: "Just kind of curious to get an update on what you're seeing" E. Gerry: "The U.S. market has been exceptionally dynamic" and "we haven't won anything." (CFO Gerry)
  • Gregory Gibas, Northland Capital Markets: "Wondering if you could perhaps discuss the puts and takes of the guidance increase" Bradley Dodson: "We did see some Canadian turnaround activity be pulled forward into the third" and "we have about $1 million of expenses that are related to these mobilizations." (CEO Dodson)
  • Gregory Gibas, Northland Capital Markets: "Could you just maybe speak to what you're hearing from the customer base" Bradley Dodson: "We're not losing work. We're not losing market share in Australia." (CEO Dodson)
  • Stephen Gengaro, Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated: "Can you talk about those 2 factors" Bradley Dodson: "I don't believe that... [oil price] is something that is truly driving spending right now." (CEO Dodson)
  • David Storms, Stonegate Capital Partners: "Just want to maybe start with the Canada integrated services and the margin profile" Bradley Dodson: "It is Ontario ramping." (CEO Dodson)

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts slightly positive, with emphasis on pricing upside and Canada inflection, including "the most optimistic I've heard you on Canada" (Stephen Gengaro, Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated) alongside probing on Australia softness.
  • Management slightly positive in prepared remarks, anchored by "we are raising our full year guidance" (CEO Dodson), while using more caution on Australia and project timing, including "we are not in the business of forecasting FID timing" (CEO Dodson).
  • Compared with last quarter, management language shifted from holding guidance to raising it, while maintaining similar caution on timing outside its control, including in Q2: "While the pace and timing of these opportunities are dependent on customer and final investment decisions" (CEO Dodson).

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Guidance moved from unchanged to higher, with Q2 stating: "we are maintaining our revenue guidance range of $675 million to $700 million" (CEO Dodson) versus Q3: "we are raising our full year 2026 revenue... to $710 million to $720 million" (CEO Dodson).
  • Canada demand framing tightened from pipeline visibility to contracted deployment, with Q2 highlighting: "We have 2,700 mobile camp rooms... that are available for deployment" (CEO Dodson) versus Q3: "we have secured contracts... for... approximately 700 mobile camp fleet rooms" (CEO Dodson).
  • Australia tone became more explicit that elevated met coal prices are not translating into expected occupancy, with Q3: "That is not what we are seeing" (CEO Dodson) compared with Q2: "we see upside as this temporary noise dissipates" (CEO Dodson).

Risks and Concerns

  • "Diesel remains elevated, labor and other input costs are inflated." (CEO Dodson)
  • "Under Queensland progressive royalty regime, a larger share of each dollar at these prices goes to the state." (CEO Dodson)
  • "These opportunities remain dependent on customer final investment decision and the timing of meaningful financial contribution remains out of our control." (CEO Dodson)

Final Takeaway

Management described Q3 as a Canada-led outperformance that drove higher full-year 2026 guidance, while emphasizing that Western Canada capacity is tightening and that newly contracted mobile fleet deployments are shifting capital allocation toward near-term mobilization. At the same time, management characterized Australia as well contracted but operating through a cost- and royalty-driven soft patch in customer behavior despite high metallurgical coal prices, with integrated services growth remaining tied to its AUD 500 million run-rate target by year-end 2027.

data.title: Methanex expects $525-$550/tonne realized price in Oct-Nov while launching up to 5% buyback
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Methanex (MEOH) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "With the third quarter average realized price of $510 per tonne and produced methanol sales of 2.3 million tonnes, our third quarter adjusted EBITDA was $543 million and adjusted net income was $284 million." (President, CEO & Director Rich Sumner)
  • "The ongoing Middle East conflict continues to have an unprecedented impact on the industry... representing 30% to 35% of the internationally traded methanol in the market." (President, CEO & Director Rich Sumner)
  • "We estimate current annualized industry demand to be approximately 90 million tonnes or a reduction of 10 million to 15 million tonnes as a result of these supply pressures." (President, CEO & Director Rich Sumner)
  • "As previously disclosed, we've entered into an agreement commencing in the first quarter of 2027 to sell our remaining gas entitlements through the end of the decade and are planning to indefinitely idle the New Zealand operations at that time." (President, CEO & Director Rich Sumner)
  • "Subsequent to the third quarter, we repaid $300 million of our 2027 senior notes, and we expect to redeem the remaining $400 million in the fourth quarter." (President, CEO & Director Rich Sumner)
  • "Yesterday, we announced Board approval to initiate a normal course issuer bid under which we may purchase and cancel up to 5% of our shares outstanding." (President, CEO & Director Rich Sumner)
  • "No, there's no difficulties. I think it's the short answer." (Senior VP of Finance & CFO Dean Richardson)

Outlook

  • "For 2026, our expected equity production continues to be approximately 9 million tonnes of methanol." (President, CEO & Director Sumner)
  • "Based on October and November contract price postings and current spot pricing, we expect our average realized price range for these two months to be approximately $525 to $550 per tonne." (President, CEO & Director Sumner)
  • "Assuming current pricing levels are sustained through December and produced sales volumes are similar to those of the third quarter, we expect adjusted EBITDA to be higher in the fourth quarter than the third quarter." (President, CEO & Director Sumner)
  • Compared with Q2’s intra-quarter pricing view, management’s language shifted from "we expect our average realized price range for July and August will be approximately $460 to $485 per tonne" to an October–November range of $525–$550, alongside an explicit expectation of higher Q4 adjusted EBITDA than Q3. (President, CEO & Director Sumner)

Financial Results

  • "With the third quarter average realized price of $510 per tonne... our third quarter adjusted EBITDA was $543 million and adjusted net income was $284 million." (President, CEO & Director Sumner)
  • "The third quarter adjusted EBITDA, which includes a $10 million accrual for restructuring activities at our New Zealand operations, decreased the second quarter of 2026, primarily due to a lower average realized price." (President, CEO & Director Sumner)
  • "We continue to deliver strong production results in the third quarter with total equity methanol production of 2.1 million tonnes." (President, CEO & Director Sumner)
  • "We ended the third quarter with over $900 million in cash." (President, CEO & Director Sumner)

Q&A

  • Hassan Ahmed, Alembic Global Advisors: asked about demand destruction and supply response; President, CEO & Director Sumner said "we've seen now all coastal MTO operations shut down" and added "that's 9 million to 10 million tonnes of demand... that's out of the market today."
  • Hassan Ahmed, Alembic Global Advisors: asked how buybacks fit versus deleveraging; President, CEO & Director Sumner said "The focus of the majority of it is to deleveraging" and "we'll likely enter into the buyback with flexibility to go up... and also pull back."
  • Laurence Alexander, Jefferies: asked if high prices are delaying long-term methanol demand decisions (including ships); President, CEO & Director Sumner said "I would say not yet. The commitments to ships are still happening" and "we haven't seen an uptick in the use of methanol for those dual fuel vessels."
  • Laurence Alexander, Jefferies: asked how quickly curtailed demand returns if prices fall; President, CEO & Director Sumner said the coastal MTO sector "is there to start up" but "it would largely be based -- have to be a lower methanol price to be competitive today."
  • Matthew Blair, TPH: asked if Chile output could rise in 2027–2028 on Argentina gas trends; President, CEO & Director Sumner said "we've got more than enough pipeline capacity" but added guidance tone: "it will likely be at the more 1.4 million tonne level for Chile for '27."
  • Matthew Blair, TPH: asked if Q3 pricing benefited from selling New Zealand gas commitments; President, CEO & Director Sumner answered "No. Certainly, nothing to do with our gas" and tied strength to "a significant boost up" in Asia Pacific pricing.
  • Ben Isaacson, Scotiabank: asked about capital return beyond a 5% buyback and dividend; President, CEO & Director Sumner said on organic growth "we'd have a lot of hesitation" and on dividend policy "We remain committed to the dividend level" and "Our primary return of capital we want to deploy is through the flexible buyback."
  • Joel Jackson, BMO: asked about Beaumont outages and Egypt gas curtailments; President, CEO & Director Sumner said on Beaumont "really nothing to report" and on Egypt "we continue to run our plants at full rates."
  • Steven Hansen, Raymond James: asked why not drive leverage toward zero and whether OCI assets have further optimization; President, CEO & Director Sumner said "we think that moving -- deleveraging provides downside protection" and added on Beaumont "there could be some debottleneck opportunities" plus "We are looking at ammonia."
  • Nelson Ng, RBC: asked about paying down later-dated debt and debottlenecking; CFO Richardson said bond repayment options could be done "fairly easily through open market or tender offers" while President, CEO & Director Sumner said sustaining and small efficiency work is within "our estimate of $150 million in capital a year."
  • Hamir Patel, CIBC: asked about 2027–2028 turnarounds and potential spot exposure; President, CEO & Director Sumner said "we'll be at the higher side" of "two to three turnarounds a year" in 2027 and clarified "we're not selling on a spot basis... the pricing mechanisms have reference to spot."
  • Ahmed Abdullah, National Bank Financial: asked about improving contract terms and new customers; President, CEO & Director Sumner said "too early to say how our contracts look for next year" and "I wouldn't be expecting big changes for next year."
  • James Cannon, UBS: asked about China winter dynamics and pricing skew; President, CEO & Director Sumner said "we do tend to see winter when we start to see restrictions on coal usage" and cautioned "we do have to be careful how high we push and how much damage that does to downstream demand."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly negative to skeptical, repeatedly pressing on sustainability and capital return pacing, including "why not" questions on faster buybacks and deeper deleveraging, and scrutiny of demand destruction and operational reliability.
  • Management’s tone was confident in near-term operations and cash generation, using decisive phrasing such as "we expect" on pricing and Q4 EBITDA direction, while also emphasizing uncertainty with statements like "there remains significant uncertainty" and "we're carefully monitoring" (President, CEO & Director Sumner).
  • Versus Q2, management’s prepared-remarks tone moved from caution about tightening supply and "increasing demand rationalization will increasingly be required" to more explicit actions and shareholder return tools, including the NCIB announcement and accelerated note repayments, while keeping the uncertainty framing. (President, CEO & Director Sumner)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Guidance language shifted from Q2’s "we expect another strong quarter of earnings lower than in the second quarter due to lower pricing" to Q3’s "we expect adjusted EBITDA to be higher in the fourth quarter than the third quarter" alongside an October–November realized price range of $525–$550. (President, CEO & Director Sumner)
  • Strategic and portfolio focus evolved from Q2’s Trinidad decision ("we announced the indefinite idling of our Titan plant") to Q3’s New Zealand path ("planning to indefinitely idle the New Zealand operations") plus a new buyback framework ("up to 5% of our shares outstanding"). (President, CEO & Director Sumner)
  • Analyst focus remained centered on war-driven supply/demand volatility and capital allocation, but Q3 questions leaned more heavily into buyback sizing, dividend framing, and longer-dated debt flexibility as cash rose to "over $900 million" from Q2’s "more than $380 million". (President, CEO & Director Sumner)

Risks and Concerns

  • "There remains significant uncertainty as to how long the industry dynamics and pricing environment could last." (President, CEO & Director Sumner)
  • "We're unaware of any specific material damage to methanol production facilities in the Gulf region and the full impact of potential disruptions to regional natural gas and related infrastructure remains unclear." (President, CEO & Director Sumner)
  • Demand destruction was framed as a present balancing mechanism: "this has been balanced with the shutdown of all coastal methanol-to-olefins demand in China" and reductions "including the Middle East, Southeast Asia and India." (President, CEO & Director Sumner)
  • Capital deployment was repeatedly tied to volatility risk: "Things can change very quickly" and management kept prioritizing balance sheet resilience by directing "the majority of free cash flow towards our deleveraging targets." (President, CEO & Director Sumner)

Final Takeaway

Methanex management characterized Q3 as a high-cash-flow quarter driven by a $510-per-tonne realized price and 2.3 million tonnes of produced sales, while framing the Middle East conflict as the key driver of tight supply, elevated pricing, and demand curtailments. Into Q4, the company guided to $525–$550 per tonne realized pricing for October–November and said it expects adjusted EBITDA to be higher than Q3 if current conditions persist. Against that backdrop, management highlighted accelerated deleveraging (including $300 million repaid on 2027 notes and an expectation to redeem the remaining $400 million in Q4) and a new NCIB to repurchase up to 5% of shares, while repeatedly emphasizing uncertainty around how long current market dynamics can last.

data.title: Alliant outlines 8%+ earnings growth through 2030 as it raises 2027–2030 capex plan to $15.9B
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Alliant Energy (LNT) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "We are pleased to share strong third quarter and year-to-date results and measurable progress against our growth strategy... updated our outlook for the remainder of this year and 2027, refreshed our capital expenditure and financing plan and accelerated and extended our earnings growth expectation plans through 2030." (President, CEO & Director Lisa Barton)
  • "5 data centers support our expectation for greater than 60% contracted demand growth by 2031... Google is taking transmission service... QTS Cedar Rapids expects to complete the commissioning of their first 2 buildings later this quarter... Meta is taking distribution service with an expectation to take transmission service Q1 '27." (President, CEO & Director Barton)
  • "Our refreshed capital investment plan through 2030 is 19% higher than last year's plan... supports an acceleration of our long-term earnings growth rate to 8% plus from 2027 through 2030." (President, CEO & Director Barton)
  • "Earlier this week, the U.S. Department of Energy announced it had closed on a $5.1 billion guaranteed loan program with Alliant Energy... we estimate up to $1.2 billion of cumulative customer savings when compared to traditional debt financing." (President, CEO & Director Barton)
  • "Yesterday, we reported third quarter 2026 GAAP earnings of $1.52 per share." (Executive VP & CFO Robert Durian)
  • "We are narrowing our 2026 full year ongoing earnings guidance to the top half of our original guidance range, which is $3.41 to $3.46 per share." (Executive VP & CFO Durian)

Outlook

  • "Our 2027 full year ongoing earnings guidance of $3.63 to $3.73 per share represents 8% growth over the midpoint of our original 2026 earnings guidance." (Executive VP & CFO Durian)
  • "We raised our long-term annual earnings growth target to 6% to 8% plus, and increased and extended our expectations to 8% plus from 2027 through 2030." (Executive VP & CFO Durian)
  • "Our 2027 annual common stock dividend target is $2.25 per share, a 5% increase over our 2026 annual dividend target... We are moderating the pace of dividend growth to help fund our larger capital plan efficiently." (Executive VP & CFO Durian)
  • "We recently filed a large load tariff in Wisconsin and an ICR application for a second Google project in Cedar Rapids and expect decisions back on both in the first half of 2027." (Executive VP & CFO Durian)

Financial Results

  • "Yesterday, we reported third quarter 2026 GAAP earnings of $1.52 per share." (Executive VP & CFO Durian)
  • "The year-over-year third quarter increase in ongoing earnings... [was] primarily driven by higher revenue requirements and AFUDC associated with capital investments... timing of income tax expense, which will reverse in the fourth quarter and have no impact on full year results." (Executive VP & CFO Durian)
  • "These positive drivers were partially offset by... higher other operations and maintenance expenses... and higher financing and depreciation costs associated with our growing rate base." (Executive VP & CFO Durian)
  • "Our refreshed capital investment plan for 2027 through 2030 totaled $15.9 billion, a 19% increase above our prior 4-year plan." (Executive VP & CFO Durian)

Q&A

  • Nicholas Campanella, Barclays Bank PLC, Research Division: "Is '27 kind of the new base to grow 8% plus off of?" Robert Durian: "You could either take the midpoint of the original guidance for 2026, which is $3.41 or the new guidance for 2027 of $3.68... think of the plus sign is representing earnings growth of at least 8% each year over the 2027 through 2030 planning period."
  • Rinny Singh, BofA Securities, Research Division: "...for that next gigawatt, the capital intensity to serve that..." Robert Durian: "...for every gigawatt of additional load, you're probably going to see somewhere in the neighborhood of $2 billion to $3 billion of additional CapEx."
  • Julien Dumoulin-Smith, Jefferies LLC, Research Division: "...more of a structural thing... on the O&M..." Robert Durian: "Think of that as we're very focused on ensuring that we have strong reliability... Those costs are going to continue to increase because we have more facilities to be able to maintain... from a pull-forward perspective, not significant amounts."
  • Paul Fremont, Ladenburg Thalmann & Co. Inc., Research Division: "...is Mesabi included now in the 2 to 4 gigawatts..." Lisa Barton: "So the 2 to 4... continues to be data center growth. So Mesabi is not included in that."
  • Anthony Crowdell, Mizuho Securities USA LLC, Research Division: "...how much cushion do you have..." Robert Durian: "...there's about 1.2 gigawatts of energy storage built into the plan... It gives us a high level of confidence to be able to navigate the plan... through the 2030 period."
  • Andrew Weisel, Scotiabank Global Banking and Markets, Research Division: "...help me bridge that gap" on equity. Robert Durian: "...there's about $600 million or $700 million that we're going to actually execute here before the end of the year... when you add that $700 million to the $2.7 billion... you actually get up to $3.4 billion of future equity."
  • Aditya Gandhi, Wolfe Research, LLC: "...how much of that [next 1 GW]... within the current planning period... and is 40% a good rule of thumb..." Robert Durian: "...the ramp rate... is actually going to start more in that '29, '30 time frame... some of that CapEx... in the '31 and beyond time frame... we actually think... funded with a relatively lower level of new common equity than our previous guidance of 40% to 50%."

Sentiment Analysis

  • "Appreciate the time and nicely done as always" and repeated clarification questions on growth math, equity bridge, and capital intensity reflected slightly positive-to-neutral analyst tone, with precision-seeking follow-ups like "help me bridge that gap." (Andrew Weisel, Scotiabank Global Banking and Markets)
  • "We have an extreme level of confidence in our ability to secure the generation that we need" and "High level of confidence in our ability to execute" reflected positive management tone, with detailed framing around inclusion criteria and pacing. (President, CEO & Director Barton)
  • Compared with Q2, management’s posture shifted from "reaffirmed 2026 full year earnings guidance" to "narrowing our 2026 full year ongoing earnings guidance" and initiating 2027 guidance and a dividend target, while analysts shifted from political/moratorium concerns in Q2 to financing mechanics and growth-rate construct in Q3. (Executive VP & CFO Durian; President, CEO & Director Barton)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • "Yesterday... narrowed our 2026 full year earnings guidance, initiated 2027 earnings guidance and dividend target and provided our updated capital expenditure and financing plans through 2030" contrasted with Q2’s "reaffirmed 2026 full year earnings guidance" and a then-outlook that "we expect compound annual earnings growth across 2027 through 2029 to be 7% plus." (Manager of Investor Relations Susan Gille; Executive VP & CFO Durian)
  • "...supports an acceleration of our long-term earnings growth rate to 8% plus from 2027 through 2030" contrasted with Q2’s framing of updating the plan on the Q3 call, and Q3 delivered that update with "$15.9 billion" for 2027–2030. (President, CEO & Director Barton; Executive VP & CFO Durian)
  • In Q2, analyst questions emphasized Iowa/Wisconsin politics and moratorium noise; in Q3, questions concentrated on the "plus" definition, equity timing, and the "$2 billion to $3 billion" per incremental gigawatt CapEx heuristic. (Shahriar Pourreza, Wells Fargo; Nicholas Campanella, Barclays)

Risks and Concerns

  • "As large load projects have increased in scale and complexity, we are raising the bar" including new gating around "local permitting" to avoid "overpromise and under deliver." (President, CEO & Director Barton)
  • "The difference between the projected 13% CAGR and our earnings growth target... primarily reflects... estimated dilution from equity issuances" and refinancing, with mitigation framed as "hybrid financing instruments" and "disciplined common equity issuances." (Executive VP & CFO Durian)
  • "Those costs are going to continue to increase" on O&M tied to an "expanded generation fleet," with management positioning this as reliability-driven. (Executive VP & CFO Durian)

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q3 2026 as a pivot to higher-visibility, large-load-driven growth, highlighted by narrowing 2026 ongoing EPS guidance to $3.41–$3.46, initiating 2027 ongoing EPS guidance of $3.63–$3.73 with a $2.25 dividend target, and extending an "8% plus" earnings-growth expectation through 2030 supported by a $15.9B 2027–2030 capital plan, DOE-backed financing, and stricter project-inclusion criteria intended to keep execution and affordability aligned.

data.title: Arbor Realty signals $700M cash by end of Q1 as it targets resolving $400M-$500M of legacy loans per quarter
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Arbor Realty Trust (ABR) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "Since that time, we've seen a tremendous increase in interest rates with the 5- and 10-year treasury indexes up another 75 to 85 basis points and 140 to 160 basis points in the last 9 months" (Chairman, President & CEO Ivan Kaufman). "This is a very material development" that he said has driven "further reductions in values across the multifamily sector of between 5% to 15%" and "significantly curtailed transaction volumes," which he said would mean "a temporary increase in our delinquencies" and "an increase in our loan loss reserves due to a change in values" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman).

  • "Our Board has decided to suspend the quarterly common dividend effective immediately, which will preserve $31 million a quarter or $125 million in annual cash flow" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman). He tied the decision to a liquidity plan: "We are currently sitting on approximately $400 million of cash and believe we can organically create another $300 million of liquidity over the next 4 to 5 months" and "anticipate that this will put our cash position at around $700 million by the end of the first quarter" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman).

  • "We ended the third quarter with approximately $750 million of delinquencies and around $500 million of REO assets for total nonperforming assets of roughly $1.25 billion" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman). He said this was "up around $200 million from last quarter's numbers" and reiterated the resolution pace: "remain confident in our ability to continue to make progress and reduce this exposure significantly over the next 4 to 6 quarters" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman).

  • "In the third quarter, we produced distributable earnings of $14.8 million or $0.08 a share, excluding realized losses of $21.7 million from the resolution of certain delinquent and REO assets that we had previously reserved for" (Executive VP & CFO Paul Elenio). "These realized losses were in the range that we guided for last quarter of $20 million to $30 million" and he added, "we anticipate our earnings to likely bottom out over the next 2 quarters" (Executive VP & CFO Elenio).

Outlook

  • "We remain confident in our ability to continue to make progress and reduce this exposure significantly over the next 4 to 6 quarters" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman). "We have a $2 billion of this book we have been aggressively working through with the goal of restructuring and resolving approximately $400 million to $500 million of loans a quarter" and he said this "will reduce our legacy book... down to around $2.7 billion by year-end at around $1 billion by the end of 2027" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman).

  • "We are targeting between $3.5 billion and $4 billion of total volume this year" in the agency business, while noting "the elevated rate environment is greatly affecting our origination executions" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman). He also described balance-sheet lending as intentionally constrained: "We have been relatively inactive in screening new business" and called this "our ongoing strategy over the next few quarters" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman).

  • Guidance language shifted with rates: "we expect this trend to likely continue for a little longer, which could continue to affect our core earnings in the short term" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman), and "given the drastic recent change in the interest rate environment, we anticipate our earnings to likely bottom out over the next 2 quarters" (Executive VP & CFO Elenio).

Financial Results

  • "We had approximately $450 million of new delinquencies" and "around a $4 million of back accrued interest being reversed and a reduction of around $6 million in interest income for a $10 million impact to interest income this quarter from these assets" (Executive VP & CFO Elenio). He also cited incremental funding costs: "We also incurred approximately $7 million of additional interest expense from issuing our convertible debt offering and leveraging up our balance sheet" (Executive VP & CFO Elenio).

  • "In the third quarter, we recorded an additional $34 million of impairment on our REO book" and "booked another $27 million of specific reserves on our balance sheet loan book for total REO impairment and specific reserves of $61 million" (Executive VP & CFO Elenio). He added, "General CECL was also elevated this quarter... resulting in an additional $27 million in reserves" and said "we expect that we could experience similar levels of reserves and impairments over the next few quarters" (Executive VP & CFO Elenio).

  • "Our book value per share came in at $10.92 at September 30" (Executive VP & CFO Elenio). In the agency segment, he reported "margins on these loans came in at 1.12% this quarter compared to 1.33% last quarter" and said the servicing portfolio was "$36.8 billion" with "an estimated remaining life of 5.6 years" and "around $128 million gross annually" of expected servicing income (Executive VP & CFO Elenio).

Q&A

  • Christopher Muller, Citizens JMP Securities, LLC, Research Division: "the $35 million of REO disposition stands out" and asked if more REO could be sold; Executive VP & CFO Elenio: "it's related to one specific asset... We have a contract signed" and "we'd be picking up $35 million of recovered equity" and added, "in October, we took a loan back already it was $70 million" (Executive VP & CFO Elenio).

  • Christopher Muller, Citizens JMP Securities, LLC, Research Division: asked whether the rate spike slows foreclosures and what 10-year level unlocks activity; Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman: "it slowed the process... between 30 and 90 days" and "you'll see a 10% to 20% drop in potential valuation" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman). Executive VP & CFO Elenio: "Going from 4.5% to 5. 30% was draconian dramatic" and "going from 5. 30% now below 5%, you'll start to see momentum come back" (Executive VP & CFO Elenio).

  • Richard Shane, JPMorgan Chase & Co, Research Division: asked about value declines by class/market; Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman: "Class A may be down 5% to 10% in good markets" but "in weaker markets... could be 15% to 25%" and referenced concessions like "3- to 4-month concessions" in certain Sun Belt markets (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman).

  • Jade Rahmani, Keefe, Bruyette, & Woods, Inc., Research Division: asked about SFR special mention loans and capital actions; Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman: "We don't look at special mention as a category that is overly concerning" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman). Executive VP & CFO Elenio: "we'll evaluate all options and alternatives" and "we are constantly evaluating that internally and with our bankers" (Executive VP & CFO Elenio). On selling an agency interest, Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman: "We haven't considered selling an interest" but "There's always options when you have good assets" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman).

  • Crispin Love, Piper Sandler & Co., Research Division: questioned SFR originations amid liquidity constraints and asked about preferred dividends; Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman: "that's the most attractive part of our business" and "we will be very selective" about balance-sheet use, while on preferreds he said, "We evaluate everything relative to liquidity" and "that's always a tool that's out there" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman).

Sentiment Analysis

  • "This is a very material development" and "material adverse change" framing drove a slightly negative analyst tone focused on liquidity, maturities, and asset-sale clearing levels, including questions like "what is the clearing price" and whether the company would need to "maximize liquidity" via sales (Raymond James’ Gabriel Poggi).

  • Management tone in prepared remarks was slightly negative on near-term credit and earnings, with phrases including "temporary increase in our delinquencies" and "earnings... likely bottom out over the next 2 quarters" (Executive VP & CFO Elenio), while remaining confident on execution timing: "remain confident" and "very ambitious to stick to that plan" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman).

  • Compared with last quarter’s more constructive positioning around liquidity creation and activity, management language turned more defensive and urgent in Q3, including "completely out of our control and not something we could have anticipated" regarding ICE impacts and "suspend the quarterly common dividend effective immediately" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman).

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Dividend policy and liquidity posture changed sharply: in Q3 management said, "Our Board has decided to suspend the quarterly common dividend effective immediately" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman), while Q2 centered on liquidity and accretion via capital markets and repurchases, including "We used $114 million of proceeds to buy back stock at $5.42" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman).

  • Credit trend messaging worsened: Q2 described nonperforming assets of "roughly $1.07 billion" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman), while Q3 reported "roughly $1.25 billion" and attributed the change to rates and ICE-related occupancy impacts (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman).

  • Earnings commentary shifted from stability to trough expectations: Q2 reported "distributable earnings of $31 million or $0.15 per share" (Executive VP & CFO Elenio), while Q3 reported "$0.08 a share" and added "we anticipate our earnings to likely bottom out over the next 2 quarters" (Executive VP & CFO Elenio).

  • Analysts’ focus moved from strategic alternatives and buybacks in Q2 (Citizens’ Christopher Muller asked about "strategic alternatives") to near-term liquidity mechanics in Q3, emphasizing the March maturity bridge, REO disposition timing, and preferred-dividend contingency (multiple analysts).

Risks and Concerns

  • "This will result in a temporary increase in our delinquencies" and "a slightly longer time frame to resolving certain legacy assets" as management cited higher rates and reduced values (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman). He also flagged geography-specific stress: "Jacksonville, Orlando, San Antonio, Houston and Atlanta" where ICE impacts "significantly reduced occupancy" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman).

  • Reserve and impairment risk was explicitly elevated: "we expect that we could experience similar levels of reserves and impairments over the next few quarters" (Executive VP & CFO Elenio). Management’s mitigation centered on liquidity and pacing: "preserve capital" and "operate our platform to resolve our legacy issues and preserve our book value" (Chairman, President & CEO Kaufman).

Final Takeaway

Management described a rate-driven deterioration in multifamily transaction liquidity and collateral values, leading to higher delinquencies and reserves, and responded with an immediate suspension of the common dividend to target about $700 million of cash by the end of the first quarter and cover the $275 million March maturity while retaining liquidity. Executives reiterated a 4- to 6-quarter timeline to work down legacy exposures by resolving $400 million to $500 million per quarter, while acknowledging near-term earnings pressure and potential for continued elevated reserve-building as dispositions and REO sales timing depend heavily on rate stability.

data.title: CNO outlines 2026 operating EPS of $5.05-$5.15 while executing $270M Bermuda life reinsurance
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: CNO Financial Group (CNO) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "CNO delivered an excellent quarter, demonstrating the strength of our diversified business model and our ability to generate consistent, repeatable results," said CEO Gary Bhojwani. "Operating earnings per diluted share were up 47% in the third quarter and up 43% year-to-date," and he added, "we are raising our full year operating earnings per share guidance and either improving or maintaining most other 2026 guidance."

  • Bhojwani highlighted continued distribution growth and mix: "We delivered our 17th consecutive quarter of sales growth and our 15th consecutive quarter of producing agent count growth," and "producing agent count grew 4%." He also tied performance to investment returns and capital returns: "New money rates have exceeded 6% for 15 consecutive quarters while maintaining a high-quality portfolio," and "we maintained a robust capital position while returning $77 million to shareholders."

  • On Medicare and consumer trends, Bhojwani said, "Medicare Supplement NAP increased 41% in the quarter," and framed market disruption as a sales driver: "More than 3 million Medicare Advantage members will need to choose new coverage for 2027 as many leading carriers continue to exit plans, pare back benefits and/or reduce service areas."

  • CFO Paul McDonough emphasized the Bermuda strategy and Q3 profitability drivers: "Effective October 1, we ceded approximately $270 million of U.S. statutory graded benefit life reserves from Colonial Penn Life Insurance Company to our Bermuda company," and "this will be an area of focus for us in 2027, looking to settle into more of a run rate cadence in 2028 and beyond." On results, he said, "we delivered operating earnings per share of $1.90," and "expenses continue to run favorably as they have all year."

Outlook

  • "We are raising our full year operating earnings per share guidance to a range of between $5.05 to $5.15," McDonough said, adding that the increase reflected "an expense ratio of 18.6% to 18.8%," "an operating effective tax rate of approximately 20.5%," "full year fee income of approximately $25 million," and "full year free cash flow of between $220 million and $240 million."

  • Compared with the prior quarter’s guidance language, McDonough shifted from noting "no change to our full year free cash flow expectations" to setting a specific range: "We now expect full year free cash flow of between $220 million and $240 million." He also tightened the expense ratio range from Q2’s "18.8% to 19.0%" to Q3’s "18.6% to 18.8%."

Financial Results

  • McDonough attributed the quarter to margin, NII, and expense control: "We had another strong quarter, reflecting continued favorable trends in insurance product margins and net investment income, along with disciplined expense and capital management." He also disclosed the share impact: "deploying $60 million of excess capital on share repurchases in the quarter" that "contributed to a 4% reduction in weighted average diluted shares outstanding."

  • On actuarial review impacts, McDonough said, "Our annual actuarial review resulted in a $56.3 million favorable impact to operating income," and noted go-forward pattern changes including "an estimated favorable impact of approximately $3.5 million in fixed indexed annuities and $1 million in Medicare Supplement."

  • On investment income sustainability, McDonough said, "Net investment income not allocated to products increased 72%," and "the result was approximately $12 million above our long-term yield estimate," but cautioned, "we would not expect this level of contribution to continue."

Q&A

  • Randy Binner, Texas Capital Securities, Research Division: "I had a question about the guide of free cash flow that is $220 million to $240 million... what changed there?" Paul McDonough: "our original free cash flow guidance for 2026 assumed that we would somehow solve for a portion of" Bermuda excess capital, and "we ultimately solve for it in the context of the third treaty... closed on October 1."

  • Randy Binner, Texas Capital Securities, Research Division: "is it possible to isolate the capital freed up from this $270 million reinsurance transfer?" McDonough: "we certainly quantify that internally" but "we've generally not quantified it in our external remarks."

  • Joel Hurwitz, Dowling & Partners Securities, LLC: "it came in better than what you guys have guided to... provide some more color on what you're doing on the expense side?" McDonough: "There haven't been any significant initiatives" and "the current expense ratio is sustainable... there's even some room for improvement going forward."

  • Hurwitz, Dowling & Partners Securities, LLC: "have you guys taken any dividend out of that entity this year?" McDonough: "No. We haven't taken dividends out as such."

  • Ryan Krueger, Keefe, Bruyette, & Woods, Inc., Research Division: "why aren't you ceding more life business to Bermuda?" Chief Actuary Jeremy Williams: "determined that this was the right size block... it is over 600,000 policies that are involved in the transaction."

  • Krueger, Keefe, Bruyette, & Woods, Inc., Research Division: "The $70 million of TechMod costs in 2026... what you expect that to be in 2027?" McDonough: "In 2027, I think we're expecting a comparable amount."

  • Suneet Kamath, Jefferies LLC, Research Division: "are you seeing anything that would suggest maybe economic pressures could start to build and impact new production...?" CEO Gary Bhojwani: "We are not seeing anything that tells us there's going to be a material reduction in the need or demand for our services."

  • Kamath, Jefferies LLC, Research Division: "do you have in place what it takes to really take advantage of" Medicare disruption? Bhojwani: "Any time there's a dislocation... that increases the need for... advice... and that plays to our strength."

  • Francis Matten, BMO Capital Markets Equity Research: "on the ROE trend line... anything that you would expect to either like revert or normalize?" McDonough: "the outperformance has contributed about 50 basis points... That's the only specific thing that I would point to."

  • Wilma Jackson Burdis, Raymond James & Associates, Inc., Research Division: "could you talk about" Medicare Supplement morbidity and annuity assumption-review impacts? Williams: "we reflected" higher morbidity in assumptions, and "on the FIA side" assumption updates "created immediate reserve release" and "a favorable quarterly reserve impact."

  • Burdis, Raymond James & Associates, Inc., Research Division: "what types of products you're specifically focused on" in ABF? CIO Eric Johnson: "We roughly have $2 billion of private credit in total that includes ABF... about half of that," and "it's pretty much all investment grade."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analyst tone was neutral-to-skeptical, pressing on capital fungibility and Bermuda constraints, including "is it possible to isolate the capital freed up" and "why aren't you ceding more life business to Bermuda?"

  • Management tone was slightly positive in prepared remarks and more measured in Q&A; McDonough said, "we would not expect this level of contribution to continue," and on reinsurance economics added, "we've generally not quantified it in our external remarks."

  • Versus the prior quarter, management language showed more certainty on Bermuda execution (Q3: "we ceded approximately $270 million") compared with Q2’s more process-oriented framing (McDonough previously said, "a third treaty could be a part of that").

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Guidance moved higher again, with McDonough now stating, "raising our full year operating earnings per share guidance to... $5.05 to $5.15" versus Q2’s "$4.60 and $4.80."

  • The Bermuda narrative shifted from planning to completion: Q2 McDonough said, "stay tuned as that evolves," while Q3 McDonough said, "with the closing of this third treaty, we've essentially completed the transactions that we had initially contemplated."

  • Analysts remained focused on Bermuda across both calls; Q2 asked for "an update on Bermuda" and potential "moving other blocks," while Q3 questions centered on dividendability, why not cede more life, and isolating capital effects.

Risks and Concerns

  • McDonough flagged volatility risk in unallocated investment income: "we would not expect this level of contribution to continue."

  • Bhojwani highlighted D2C variability: "This strategy will create quarterly variability."

  • Williams described Medicare Supplement claims pressure: "we've seen the much higher morbidity the last several periods," and McDonough noted the annual review was "partially offset by unfavorable claims trends in Medicare Supplement."

Final Takeaway

Management described Q3 as driven by sustained sales momentum, improving expense leverage, and elevated investment income, while raising full-year operating EPS guidance to $5.05-$5.15 and setting free cash flow expectations at $220M-$240M. The call also marked execution of the third Bermuda reinsurance treaty—ceding about $270M of life reserves—while management emphasized 2027 as a year to further optimize Bermuda assets and capital, and repeatedly cautioned that unusually strong unallocated investment income is not expected to persist at the same level.

data.title: Cousins raises 2026 FFO midpoint to $2.97 as it targets 90% occupancy by year-end and plans a ~700,000-square-foot Dallas tower in 2027
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Cousins Properties (CUZ) Q3 2026

Management View

  • “We had a very strong third quarter at Cousins. We increased our earnings guidance, completed strategic transactions that will increase the quality of our portfolio, and had robust leasing and operational metrics.” (President, CEO & Director Michael Connolly)
  • “We increased FFO guidance by $0.02 a share to $2.97 per share for the full year in 2026… which represents 4.6% growth over 2025.” (President, CEO & Director Connolly)
  • “We leased 546,000 square feet during the quarter, including 220,000 square feet of new and expansion leases… we are on track to hit our 90% occupancy target by year-end.” (President, CEO & Director Connolly)
  • “Our cash rent roll-up on second-generation leasing was 19.8%, our strongest performance in 5 years. This marks 50 consecutive quarters of positive rent roll-ups.” (President, CEO & Director Connolly)
  • “Our share of the initial investment in the venture was approximately $50 million, which includes $42.2 million for the land and $7.8 million of predevelopment costs.” (Executive VP & Chief Investment Officer Jane Hicks)
  • “We currently anticipate full year ’26 FFO between $2.95 and $2.99 per share with a midpoint of $2.97. This is up $0.02 from our prior midpoint.” (Executive VP & CFO Gregg D. Adzema)

Outlook

  • “We currently anticipate full year ’26 FFO between $2.95 and $2.99 per share… The higher FFO outlook is primarily driven by better-than-forecast leasing activity and fee income.” (Executive VP & CFO Adzema)
  • “Our updated guidance also assumes that none of the shares that are issued on a forward basis settle in 2026… [and] continues to assume the sale of the 303 Tremont land parcel during the fourth quarter.” (Executive VP & CFO Adzema)
  • “It does not include any additional acquisitions, dispositions or development starts this year.” (Executive VP & CFO Adzema)
  • “Our current plan is to commence construction in 2027 on a trophy office tower with a planned size of approximately 700,000 square feet.” (President, CEO & Director Connolly)

Financial Results

  • “Third quarter same-property cash NOI increased 7.4% over last year, driven by a 5.5% revenue growth number and 2% expense growth.” (Executive VP & CFO Adzema)
  • “Excluding 201 North Tryon, same-property cash NOI for the balance of the portfolio increased 8.6% in the third quarter.” (Executive VP & CFO Adzema)
  • “For the quarter, our total office portfolio end-of-period lease and weighted average occupancy percentages were 93% and 89.5%, respectively, both up sequentially.” (Executive Vice President of Operations Richard Hickson)
  • “We also sold 917,000 shares on a forward basis under our ATM program at an average gross price of $31.37… [for] approximately $120 million… none of which have settled.” (Executive VP & CFO Adzema)

Q&A

  • Blaine Heck, Wells Fargo Securities, LLC: Asked for 2401 McKinney total spend, yield, timeline, and pre-leasing. President, CEO & Director Connolly: “We are still finalizing the building plans and the ultimate cost… based on the current time line, that’s going to be in the first half of 2027… overall construction costs… range somewhere between $900 to $1,000 a foot.”
  • Blaine Heck, Wells Fargo Securities, LLC: Asked about JV economics and interest-rate considerations. President, CEO & Director Connolly: “We have the 97.5%, 2.5% joint venture… [and] the bar for new development… is… higher… the only thing that we’ve actually committed to is buying land.”
  • Blaine Heck, Wells Fargo Securities, LLC: Asked if 19.8% roll-up had one-offs and what’s sustainable. Executive Vice President of Operations Hickson: “There really weren’t any single leases that drove the higher roll-up… it really was broad-based… we feel confident we can continue to probably achieve something in that range.”
  • Manus Ebbeck, Evercore ISI: Asked how development would be funded and 2027 impacts. Executive VP & CFO Adzema: “We’ve got 2 north stars, which is, it will be accretive and it will be leverage-neutral… $120 million of unsettled ATM shares… It’s really hard… what you should put in your model for 2027.”
  • Jana Galan, BofA Securities: Asked about occupancy “next goalpost” and balancing rate vs. fill-up. President, CEO & Director Connolly: “We were running the portfolio 92% to 93% occupied… we are also sharply focused on driving rental rates… I’m reluctant to give a specific time line.”
  • Anthony Paolone, JPMorgan: Asked about cap rates and required development spreads. President, CEO & Director Connolly: “We’ve historically looked at development… spreads of 150 to 200 basis points over spot cap rates… we probably skew towards the higher end.” Executive VP & CIO Hicks: “You’re still seeing core office assets trade in that plus or minus 7% range.”
  • John Kim, BMO: Asked about key Austin tenants and McKinney tenant announcement timing. Executive Vice President of Operations Hickson: “That really has no net impact on net operating income” (Google self-managing) and “they are absolutely very committed to their footprint” (Amazon). President, CEO & Director Connolly: “Before you can sign a lease, you have to finalize the building plans and the ultimate cost.”
  • Michael Lewis, Truist: Asked about forward equity settlement timing. Executive VP & CFO Adzema: “No, we do not have to settle those shares by the end of the year. We will much more than likely just extend an agreement with the bank for another year.”

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts sentiment was slightly positive and detail-seeking, with repeated probing on development underwriting and timing, including “total expected spend… the yield you’re underwriting” (Blaine Heck, Wells Fargo Securities, LLC).
  • Management sentiment was positive in prepared remarks and more guarded on development specifics in Q&A, including “I cannot give you… a specific total cost” (President, CEO & Director Connolly) and “hard to say right now because we don’t have specific timing” (Executive VP & CFO Adzema).
  • Versus last quarter, management language shifted from “we are hopeful to have news to share in coming quarters” (President, CEO & Director Connolly, Q2) to detailing a specific development site and timetable, including “commence construction in 2027” (President, CEO & Director Connolly, Q3).

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Guidance moved higher, from “midpoint of $2.95 per share” (President, CEO & Director Connolly, Q2) to “midpoint of $2.97” (President, CEO & Director Connolly, Q3).
  • Leasing volume stepped down from “924,000 square feet of leases” (President, CEO & Director Connolly, Q2) to “546,000 square feet” (President, CEO & Director Connolly, Q3), while pricing strengthened as “cash rent roll-up… was 19.8%” (President, CEO & Director Connolly, Q3) vs. “9.2%” (President, CEO & Director Connolly, Q2).
  • Capital-markets messaging shifted from expecting forward settlement timing (Q2) to explicitly excluding it: “none of the shares… settle in 2026” (Executive VP & CFO Adzema, Q3).
  • The largest strategic change was Dallas development visibility, moving from general “select development opportunities” (Executive VP & CIO Hicks, Q2) to “a 2.3-acre development site at 2401 McKinney” (Executive VP & CIO Hicks, Q3).

Risks and Concerns

  • “As Richard discussed earlier, this asset is currently undergoing a major redevelopment. And as a result, cash NOI was down 35% compared to last year.” (Executive VP & CFO Adzema)
  • “The new lease is expected to commence in phases starting in late 2027… So we will see some downtime in 2027.” (Executive Vice President of Operations Hickson)
  • “The recent increase in interest rates and limited equity in the office sector will likely constrain overall transaction volume in the near term.” (Executive VP & CIO Hicks)

Final Takeaway

Cousins management framed Q3 as a quarter of stronger operating results and portfolio-upgrading capital allocation, highlighted by a raised 2026 FFO outlook of $2.95 to $2.99 per share, a 90% year-end occupancy target, and a step-up in second-generation cash rent roll-ups to 19.8%. The call’s center of gravity was 2401 McKinney in Uptown Dallas, where management outlined a 97.5% owned JV land position and positioned a ~700,000-square-foot trophy tower for a potential 2027 construction start, while repeatedly emphasizing that building plans and costs are still being finalized before any leasing announcement.
